description: Canonical service_kind vocabulary. A service_kind names an independent protocol identity or trust role that a remote party must distinguish. It never classifies Station-internal processes, operation bundles, features, limits, or transport bindings. This registry is the single source of valid values and per-context eligibility for Service Describe, Realm join candidates, ServiceRegistrationKey, and the MIMI provider directory. Consumers MUST derive their closed value space from active rows whose valid_in includes the applicable context.
registry_rules: A service_kind id matches [a-z][a-z0-9_]* and is lowercase snake_case. Only ids present as rows in this registry exist; only status=active rows are valid on wire.

Value spaces are NOT interchangeable. Each row declares valid_in, the set of contexts the id may legally appear in. A service_kind valid for Service Describe is not thereby valid as a Realm join-candidate class or as a ServiceRegistrationKey component. Consumers MUST derive their enum from the rows whose valid_in contains that consumer's context, never from the full row list.
Schema enum values for every service_kind selector field MUST be generated from active rows filtered by valid_in; tools/artifact_lint check_service_kind_registry asserts each declared JSON pointer.

service_registration_key is the most restrictive context: it admits only service types that are a standalone deployment owning a service DID under a canonical public base. Adding a row to this context means that service type can hold a service identity and appear in ak.root.identity.service_registration.* operations.

New service types enter only when a remote party must distinguish an independent service DID or signature, explicit delegation or allowlist, plaintext/key/recovery/compliance boundary, direct discovered base URL, or different normative authority/state result. Process separation, scaling, private RPC, internal hostnames, compute cost, or future deployment flexibility are insufficient.

service_kind is a role name, not a product, process, module, operation bundle, feature, or transport name. Deployment or implementation identifiers (for example a binary called soland or starid) MUST NOT be registered. A single physical deployment MAY fill more than one independent role, but each ServiceDescribe document describes exactly one role. Co-located roles sharing a public binding are selected with GET /_arkret/describe?service_kind=<registered-id>; each response advertises only that role's exact supported_operation_bundles, profiles, authentication metadata, limits and plaintext visibility. Compound service_kind values are forbidden.
This registry governs service_kind selector fields, including the policy source_service_kind attribution field.

contexts.description: Top-level service_kind of a Service Describe document (schemas/service-describe.schema.json). Every deployable role may describe itself.

Service class permitted as a bounded join-forwarding target (schemas/realm-join-candidate.schema.json). v1 permits only the Station carried by an exact signed invite AccountId or projected from a current joined-member ActorId; clients never submit directly to the candidate.

The service_kind half of a ServiceRegistrationKey (service_kind + canonical public_base_url). Only roles that own a service DID under a public base belong here. Producers and validators MUST reject any service_kind absent from this context.

Provider directory descriptor of the MIMI interop surface (schemas/mimi-interop.schema.json $defs/provider_directory). Pinned as a const rather than an enum because the context admits exactly one role.

service_kinds.description: Authoritative Station for closed AccountId pairs: business data, account and Event admission, client sync, federation, authz, device/key state, queues, cursors, and Account Authority discovery. Internal Auth, policy, sync, federation, and key processes do not acquire separate service kinds. A Station may also act as an embedded did:webvh host for identities it serves.
Standalone did:webvh registry: DID documents, key logs, receipts, watcher/mirror. Self-hosts its own service DID through its local store.
Authority commit and current-state attestation surface.
Discovery ingest/query with anti-enumeration and takedown audit.
Long-term archive storage and retrieval surface.
Cryptographic key backup and recovery surface.
MIMI interop provider facade. Deliberately NOT valid_in service_describe: it names a facade role inside the MIMI provider-directory descriptor, not a standalone Arkret service describing itself.
